name: CD4051BM96
title: CMOS analog multiplexers: 8:1 (CD4051B), dual 4:1 (CD4052B) and triple 2:1 (CD4053B)
summary: Three CMOS analog multiplexer/demultiplexers with on-chip address decoding and level shifting: the CD4051B picks one of eight channels, the CD4052B one of four channel pairs, and the CD4053B sets three independent single-pole double-throw switches. Logic runs between VSS and VDD (3 V to 20 V), while the analog signal may swing from VEE to VDD, up to 20 V peak to peak. A high on INH opens every switch. Quiescent current is tens of nanoamps typical and switching is break-before-make.

circuits.title: Keypad scanning with a microcontroller
circuits.description: A microcontroller reads an eight-key pad through one CD4051B. Each key, when closed, lifts its channel to 3.3 V; a 10 kΩ resistor to ground holds the channel low otherwise. The controller sets C, B and A to each of the eight codes in turn and samples COM on a single input. VDD is at 3.3 V; INH, VEE and VSS are grounded. Any number of closed keys are detected, standby power is small and only four controller pins are used, but the scan has to run continuously and occupies the controller while it does.

circuits.title: 24-to-1 multiplexer addressing
circuits.description: Three CD4051B share the address lines A, B and C. Half of a CD4556, its E input grounded, takes the two upper address bits D and E and drives the INH inputs of the three multiplexers from Q0, Q1 and Q2, so that one multiplexer at a time is enabled. The three COM pins are joined as one common output.
notes: The decoder output Q3 is unconnected.

equations.name: VDD supply capability with separately powered signals

where.RL: effective external load on the switches

equations.note: Applies where VDD and the signal inputs come from separate supplies; meeting it prevents a standing current or clamping on the VDD rail at power-up and power-down.

operation.text: Control inputs swing between VSS and VDD; the analog path swings between VEE and VDD. With VDD - VSS = 3 V, up to 13 V of VDD - VEE can be switched; above 13 V of VDD - VEE, VDD - VSS must be at least 4.5 V. Example: VDD = +4.5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -13.5 V passes signals from -13.5 V to +4.5 V under 0 V to 5 V logic. Quiescent power stays very low over the whole supply range whatever the control inputs do.
For the address and inhibit inputs, logic 0 is VSS and logic 1 is VDD. The signal through each transmission gate may run anywhere from VEE to VDD.

CD4051B: three binary address inputs A, B, C and an inhibit pick one of eight channels onto COM. CD4052B: two address inputs A, B and an inhibit pick one of four X/Y channel pairs, a differential 4-channel multiplexer. CD4053B: three separate selects A, B, C each set one single-pole double-throw switch; one inhibit serves all three.
A logic 1 on INH turns every channel off, whatever the address.
The switches pass signals both ways: used as a demultiplexer, COM is the input and the channel pins are the outputs.
On a change of address the old channel opens before the new one closes, so two channels are never on together.
Every input has the standard CMOS protection network.

Keep inputs within 0.5 V above VDD and below VEE, and do not pull outputs above VDD or below VEE. Control thresholds are the VIH and VIL limits, and switching times the propagation delays, of the electrical characteristics.
The switches have no drive circuitry: they neither source nor sink current, and any current flowing is simply passed through the channel.

The CMOS stages have balanced drive. Two outputs driving one bus against each other can pass currents beyond the maximum ratings, and strong drive into a light load gives fast edges that may ring; routing and loading have to allow for both.

Any supply within the minimum and maximum ratings is allowed. Bypassing: 0.1 µF on a single-supply part; 0.01 µF or 0.022 µF on each VCC pin where several VCC pins are joined internally; 0.1 µF on each supply pin of a dual-supply part. Two capacitors in parallel, commonly 0.1 µF and 1 µF, cover different noise frequencies. The capacitor goes as close to its power pin as possible.

A trace turned through a sharp 90° corner widens to 1.414 times its width at the apex, which disturbs its line impedance and causes reflections. A chamfered corner is better; a rounded corner that keeps the width constant is best.
Built-in ESD protection is limited: store or handle the parts with their leads shorted together or in conductive foam to protect the MOS gates.
Automotive versions are the CD4051B-Q1 and CD4053B-Q1; military versions are the CD4051B-MIL, CD4052B-MIL and CD4053B-MIL.
